processes.name: Autocatalysis
processes.description: DRAFT — Autocatalysis — a self-reinforcing reaction set.  ·  senses: the available substrate concentrations.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: AutocatalysisODE
processes.description:
Self-organised grain: an autocatalytic cycle producing product and catalyst
from substrate. products = k · substrates ; catalysts = k_cat · substrates.

processes.name: BiofilmGrowth
processes.description: DRAFT — Biofilm growth — the community grows into a structured biofilm.  ·  senses: the embedded-cell population; the matrix; nutrient availability.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: BiofilmGrowthProc
processes.description:
Biofilm mass grows on nutrients, and the ECM-embedded population expands:
d[mass]/dt = k·cells·nutrients ; d[cells]/dt = g·cells·ecm.

processes.name: CatalyzedReactionNetwork
processes.description: DRAFT — Catalyzed reaction network — the fine-grained mechanism.  ·  senses: substrate and catalyst (enzyme) concentrations.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: CellMetabolism
processes.description: DRAFT — Cell metabolism — nutrients converted to metabolites + energy.  ·  senses: the cytoplasmic nutrient and enzyme pools.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: CellMetabolismODE
processes.description:
Enzyme-catalysed conversion of imported nutrients into metabolites + energy:
rate = k · nutrients · enzymes (enzymes catalytic, not consumed).

processes.name: CellularInterface
processes.description: DRAFT — The minimal cellular interface — physical + cellular ports.  ·  senses: external chemical, mechanical, electrical, and thermal state.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: CellularInterfaceHandler
processes.description:
A bounded, goal-directed cell at its interface: it takes up chemical
supply (Monod), grows and accretes volume + a biomass-proxy objective, keeps
its viability up while its thermal environment stays within tolerance, and
passes its physical exchange ports (force, current, heat flux, signaling)
through plausible linear responses to their drivers.

processes.name: CoarseGrainedMetabolism
processes.description: DRAFT — Coarse-grained metabolism — the whole network as one exchange.  ·  senses: the incoming nutrient flux delivered across the boundary.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: CoarseMetabolism
processes.description:
Coarse grain: the whole network lumped into linear yields on the nutrient
supply (dX/dt = Y · nutrients).

processes.name: ContainmentClosure
processes.description: DRAFT — Containment closure — maintains a boundary that defines inside/outside.  ·  senses: the available lipid concentration.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: ContainmentClosureODE
processes.description:
Coarse grain: membrane boundary area accretes from the lipid pool, and the
permeability level saturates with available lipid (set-semantics).

processes.name: ContainmentODE
processes.description:
Assemble membrane area from the lipid pool: dA/dt = k · lipids. Lipids act
as the supply driver (held by the environment), so membrane area grows first
order in available lipid concentration.

processes.name: DNAReplication
processes.description: DRAFT — DNA replication — duplicates the chromosome before division.  ·  senses: current chromosomal DNA content; available free energy.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: DNAReplicationODE
processes.description: Autocatalytic DNA replication driven by free energy: d[dna]/dt = k·dna·energy.

processes.name: Diffusion
processes.description: DRAFT — Diffusion — relaxes metabolite gradients.  ·  senses: the metabolite concentration field.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: DiffusionRelax
processes.description:
Diffusion over a SINGLE lumped metabolite store cannot relax to a spatial
mean (there is no neighbouring cell to exchange with), so this handler stands
in for transport loss with a mild first-order turnover:
d[metabolites]/dt = -d · metabolites. It removes metabolites at a rate
proportional to their concentration, opposing metabolism's production so the
shared pool reaches a moving balance rather than growing without bound.

processes.name: DisintegrationEvent
processes.description:
Rewrite (Fig 6): on the ``disintegrating`` flag, the maintained boundary
fails — biomass decays into molecular debris (cell → molecular components).

processes.name: DivisionEvent
processes.description:
Rewrite (Fig 10): on the ``dividing`` flag, partition biomass into two
daughters ONCE and increment the cell count.

processes.name: DivisionRewrite
processes.description:
Event-driven division. Tracks an internal cell-cycle clock; once it reaches
``division_time`` the cell divides ONCE — the parent biomass is partitioned
equally into the two daughters and the cell count increments. A discrete
rewrite event realised over the run (before the event: nothing; at the event:
the partition). Conformance is checked against the wiring (``REWRITE``).

processes.name: ECMSecretion
processes.description: DRAFT — ECM secretion — attached cells build the extracellular matrix.  ·  senses: the attached-cell population; the metabolite pool.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: ECMSecretionProc
processes.description: Attached cells secrete extracellular matrix: d[ecm]/dt = k·cells·metabolites.

processes.name: ElectricalSignaling
processes.description: DRAFT — Electrical signaling — information exchange via charge.  ·  senses: the membrane potential.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: FBAMetabolism
processes.description:
Real flux-balance-analysis metabolism (COBRApy). Same signature as the Fig 6
coarse/kinetic handlers — ``nutrients ⇒ biomass, energy, entropy, secretions`` —
but the biomass flux is the LP optimum of a small metabolic network whose
nutrient-uptake bound is driven by the incoming flux each step (a minimal dFBA
step).

processes.name: GeneExpression
processes.description: DRAFT — Gene expression — reads genes and makes proteins/enzymes.  ·  senses: the gene pool and the amino-acid building-block pool.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: GeneExpressionODE
processes.description:
Translate the gene template, drawing on amino-acid building blocks, into
proteins and enzymes: rate = k · genes · amino_acids, split into a protein
and an enzyme yield. This is the sole source of the enzyme pool metabolism
reads, and of the protein pool.

processes.name: Growth
processes.description: DRAFT — Growth — conversion of uptake into biomass.  ·  senses: the net substrate flux delivered by exchange/metabolism.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: KineticMetabolism
processes.description:
Fine grain, same interface: a saturating (Michaelis–Menten) uptake law
standing in for resolved enzyme kinetics, coarse-grained back to the cell's
nutrient→biomass exchange ports. Same signature as CoarseMetabolism, different
dynamics — the demonstration of handler independence (law #4).

processes.name: KineticReactionNetwork
processes.description:
Molecular grain: mass-action kinetics for the catalyzed reaction network.
signature CatalyzedReactionNetwork: in {substrates, catalysts} → out {products}.

processes.name: LipidAggregation
processes.description: DRAFT — Lipid aggregation — lipid monomers aggregate.  ·  senses: the lipid-monomer concentration.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: LipidAggregationODE
processes.description: Molecular grain: lipid monomers aggregate into micelle/bilayer counts.

processes.name: MassActionReactions
processes.description:
Generic mass-action interconversion of building blocks: reaction rate
r = k · amino_acids · nucleic_acids assembles proteins (protein_yield · r)
and turns over the nucleic-acid pool (consumes nucleic_turnover · r of it).
Replication feeds nucleic acids in; these reactions draw them back down —
the interconversion loop that keeps the building-block stores balanced.

processes.name: MechanicalRelax
processes.description:
Relax the (scalar) mechanical field toward the barrier-imposed
equilibrium: dσ/dt = relax_rate · (barriers − σ).

processes.name: MechanicalStress
processes.description: DRAFT — Mechanical stress — force fields and physical barriers.  ·  senses: the environmental force field and barrier configuration.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MembraneSelfAssembly
processes.description: DRAFT — Membrane self-assembly — amphiphiles assemble into a bilayer.  ·  senses: the lipid concentration available to assemble.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MembraneSelfAssemblyODE
processes.description: Self-organised grain: membrane area self-assembles first-order in lipid.

processes.name: MetabolismClosure
processes.description: DRAFT — Metabolism closure — sustains chemical stores far from equilibrium.  ·  senses: incoming nutrient flux and available free energy.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MetabolismClosureODE
processes.description:
Coarse grain: lumped nutrient→metabolite yield with entropy production.
metabolites = yield · nutrients ; entropy = entropy_rate · nutrients.

processes.name: MetabolismLinear
processes.description:
Enzyme-catalysed conversion of nutrients into metabolites and free energy.
Flux = k · enzymes · nutrients (enzymes catalytic, not consumed); metabolites
and energy are produced at fixed yields on that flux. Enzymes start at zero,
so metabolism only fluxes once gene expression has made some — the coupling
that makes the cell mutually dependent.

processes.name: MinimalCellContainment
processes.description: DRAFT — Minimal-cell containment — maintains the membrane from lipids.  ·  senses: the lipid pool.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MinimalCellMetabolism
processes.description: DRAFT — Minimal-cell metabolism — enzymes turn nutrients into metabolites and energy.  ·  senses: the enzyme pool and the available nutrients.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MinimalCellReplication
processes.description: DRAFT — Minimal-cell replication — copies the gene pool using energy.  ·  senses: the gene pool and the available free energy.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MolecularMechanism
processes.description: DRAFT — Molecular mechanism — a process over typed physical channels.  ·  senses: incoming chemical, electrical, mechanical, and thermal flows, read against its molecular structure.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: MolecularMechanismHandler
processes.description:
A molecular mechanism as a channel transducer: chemical turnover with heat
dissipation, plus Ohmic (electrical) and elastic (mechanical) pass-through.

processes.name: MotileForce
processes.description: DRAFT — Motile force generation — mechanical output for movement.  ·  senses: internal available energy.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: NutrientExchange
processes.description: DRAFT — Nutrient exchange — chemical flux across the cell boundary.  ·  senses: external nutrient concentration; available boundary area.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: PortAddition
processes.description: DRAFT — Port addition — a compositional innovation adding an interface port.  ·  senses: the genome sequence encoding the new capability.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: PortAdditionProc
processes.description:
Evolution adds a new interface capability: a previously-silent chemical
exchange port turns on and ramps to its capacity flux. The new port going from
zero to nonzero is the executable signature of 'a new port is added' (Fig 10f).

processes.name: ProductionDegradation
processes.description: DRAFT — Production / degradation — chemical sources and sinks.  ·  senses: the environmental chemical field.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: ProductionDegradationField
processes.description:
A localized source injecting chemical at one grid cell plus first-order
decay everywhere: dfield/dt = source·δ(source_index) − k·field.

processes.name: ReactionDiffusion
processes.description: DRAFT — Reaction–diffusion — spreads and transforms chemical fields.  ·  senses: the environmental chemical field.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: Reactions
processes.description: DRAFT — Reactions — generic molecular reactions among building blocks.  ·  senses: the amino-acid and nucleic-acid building-block pools.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: ReplicationAndRepair
processes.description: DRAFT — Replication & repair — DNA is copied and maintained.  ·  senses: the nuclear DNA pool, gene content, and accumulated damage.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: ReplicationAndRepairODE
processes.description:
Grow/maintain the DNA pool from the gene template: rate = k · genes
(first-order template-directed replication and repair).

processes.name: ReplicationClosure
processes.description: DRAFT — Replication closure — maintains and copies template information.  ·  senses: the template sequence and the available free energy.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: ReplicationClosureODE
processes.description:
Coarse grain: template-directed copying driven by free energy. copies =
k · energy ; the template is conserved (declared, not rewritten).

processes.name: ReplicationODE
processes.description:
Copy the gene pool by spending free energy: rate = k · genes · energy.
Gene copies are added back to the gene store (autocatalytic growth) and
nucleic-acid building blocks are returned as a byproduct of copying. Energy
is the driver supplied by metabolism.

processes.name: SegregateChromosome
processes.description: DRAFT — Chromosome segregation — partitions replicated DNA to the poles.  ·  senses: the replicated (roughly doubled) DNA pool.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: SegregateChromosomeProc
processes.description:
Segregate replicated DNA toward the two daughter poles: each daughter's DNA
accretes a fraction of the parent's DNA per step (dna_1 = dna_2 = seg·dna).

processes.name: Selection
processes.description: DRAFT — Selection — favors viable interfaces, eliminates those that fail.  ·  senses: each variant's viability and its fitness objective value.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: SelectionProc
processes.description:
Selection expands the population by viability-weighted fitness:
d[cell_count]/dt = k·viability·fitness.

processes.name: SingleCellProcesses
processes.description: DRAFT — Single-cell processes — the cell's side of the coupling.  ·  senses: local chemical and mechanical fields at the cell's location.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: SingleCellSpatial
SpatialDiffusion
processes.description:
Real spatial diffusion on the chemical grid: returns the diffusion delta
``D · ∇²field · interval`` (zero-flux edges). Mass-conserving.

processes.name: SubunitAssembly
processes.description: DRAFT — Subunit assembly — subunits assembled into complexes.  ·  senses: the cytoplasmic protein pool and the free ribosomal-subunit count.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: SubunitAssemblyODE
processes.description:
Assemble ribosomes from proteins + ribosomal subunits: rate = k · proteins ·
ribosomal_subunits. Closes the loop back to translation.

processes.name: SurfaceAttachment
processes.description: DRAFT — Surface attachment — cells adhere to a surface.  ·  senses: the free-cell population; the available surface area.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: SurfaceAttachmentProc
processes.description:
Cells attach to the surface (saturating in surface area) and build adhesion
force proportional to the attached population.

processes.name: TemplateDirectedSynthesis
processes.description: DRAFT — Template-directed synthesis — monomers polymerize along a template.  ·  senses: the monomer concentration and the template sequence.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: TemplateDirectedSynthesisProc
processes.description:
Molecular grain: monomers polymerise on a template into a (string) polymer.
The polymer product is structural (a sequence), so this handler has no numeric
output — it is the deliberately-inert molecular grain; the composite evolves
through the other seven handlers.

processes.name: TemplateReplication
processes.description: DRAFT — Template replication — a template directs its own copying.  ·  senses: the template sequence.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: TemplateReplicationODE
processes.description: Self-organised grain: constant-rate copying while the template is present.

processes.name: ThermalEnvironment
processes.description:
Drives the environmental temperature: a baseline, then a thermal shock after
``shock_time`` — the perturbation that pushes the cell past its viability bound.

processes.name: Transcription
processes.description: DRAFT — Transcription — genes read from DNA into RNA.  ·  senses: chromosomal DNA, its gene loci, and the regulation complex.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: TranscriptionODE
processes.description:
Transcribe DNA into RNA at a gene-templated rate, damped by the regulation
complex: rate = k · dna · genes / (1 + regulation).

processes.name: Translation
processes.description: DRAFT — Translation — RNA read on ribosomes into protein.  ·  senses: cytoplasmic RNA, the metabolite (amino-acid) pool, and the available ribosome count.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: TranslationODE
processes.description:
Translate RNA into protein on the ribosome pool, drawing on metabolite
building blocks: rate = k · rna · ribosome · (metabolites / (km + metabolites)).

processes.name: TransmembraneTransport
processes.description: DRAFT — Transmembrane transport — matter moved across the membrane.  ·  senses: external nutrient concentration and the membrane transporter pool.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: TransmembraneTransportODE
processes.description:
Import nutrients across the membrane at a transporter-catalysed rate:
flux = k · nutrients_ext · transporters. The imported flux fills the cytoplasmic
nutrient pool (and a little metabolite), and is reported on the flux port.

processes.name: Uptake
processes.description:
Cell–environment coupling (Fig 5): import nutrients from the environment
reservoir into the cell's local pool: d[local]/dt = k · nutrients_ext.

processes.name: Variation
processes.description: DRAFT — Variation — discrete driving events expand functional diversity.  ·  senses: the current genome sequence.  ·  status: draft - no update dynamics yet

processes.name: VariationProc
processes.description:
Genomic variation is structural (sequence/identity strings), so this handler
has no numeric output — the variation is realised as the new identity in the
variant compartment; the composite evolves through selection + port addition.

processes.name: ViabilityGatedMetabolism
processes.description:
Metabolism (Fig 6), gated by viability: flux = k · nutrients_local · viability.
Grows biomass + energy, consumes the local nutrient. When viability → 0 (out of
bounds) the flux vanishes — growth halts, as the paper requires.

processes.name: ViabilityMonitor
processes.description:
The interface's viability logic (Fig 4). Relaxes viability toward 1 inside the
thermal tolerance band and toward 0 outside it, and raises two event flags:
``dividing`` when biomass crosses the division threshold while healthy, and
``disintegrating`` when viability falls below the survival floor.

processes.name: Analysis
processes.description:
Live-``conn`` analysis base: reads sim output via a DuckDB connection +
the ParCa ``sim_data``, and emits a rendered ``view`` (HTML) plus optional
``data`` (map). Faithful native ports of vEcoli's ``plot()`` analyses build
on this base (cf. the record-based ``AnalysisStep`` for emitted-observable
analyses). Subclasses set ``scale`` + ``name`` and implement ``analyze``.

Live, non-serializable handles (``conn``, ``sim_data``) are injected by the
runner into the state dict passed to ``update``; ``inputs()`` declares them
for discoverability with a permissive ("any") type.

Genuinely distinct from ``AnalysisStep`` (its parent only for the shared
``scale``/registry machinery via ``__init_subclass__``) — this is NOT a
thin alias. v2ecoli's production ``analysis_runner.py::run_analyses()``
drives ~30 concrete subclasses through exactly this surface (calling
``update()`` with ``conn``/``history_sql``/``sim_data``/... injected
directly into ``state``, bypassing ``ResultsHandle`` entirely), so
``update()`` here must read those keys straight off ``state`` — it must
NOT read a ``ResultsHandle`` from ``state["results"]`` the way
``AnalysisStep.update()`` does. (A prior collapse of this base into
``AnalysisStep`` silently dropped the injected conn/history_sql/sim_data
kwargs, breaking all ~30 subclasses; restored here to the original
pre-collapse behavior.)

processes.name: AnalysisStep
processes.description:
Canonical base for post-sim analyses.

Reads the ``ResultsHandle`` that ``ResultsStep`` wrote to the ``results``
store and implements ``analyze(rows) -> dict`` over
``results.records(scale=self.scale)``. Subclasses that need direct SQL
access instead of record dicts can pull ``results.conn()`` (lazy DuckDB)
or ``results.sim_data`` from within ``analyze`` (the handle is available
via the ``results`` input if a subclass overrides ``update`` to keep it).
Subclasses set ``scale`` (one of ``ANALYSIS_SCALES``) + ``name``.

``Analysis`` (below) is a *separate*, genuinely distinct base for the
live-``conn`` surface v2ecoli's ``analysis_runner.py`` drives directly —
it only shares ``__init_subclass__``'s ``scale``/registry machinery with
this class, not ``update()``/``inputs()``/``outputs()``. (An earlier
revision collapsed ``Analysis`` into a thin alias of this class, which
silently dropped the injected ``conn``/``history_sql``/``sim_data``
kwargs and broke every v2ecoli ``Analysis`` subclass; do not repeat
that — the two bases stay distinct.) For backward compatibility,
``update()`` here also accepts a plain list in the ``results`` store
(the pre-``ResultsHandle`` contract) — used as-is, no handle required.

processes.name: ConsoleEmitter
processes.description: Print state to console each timestep.

processes.name: Distribution
processes.description:
Histogram of an observable's distribution.

Inputs (declared types):
  samples: list[float] — the values to bin

processes.name: Heatmap
processes.description:
Color matrix over a 2D parameter sweep.

Inputs (declared types):
  x_params: list[float]
  y_params: list[float]
  z_values: list[list[float]]  — z[y_idx][x_idx]

processes.name: InvestigationAnalysisStep
processes.description:
One investigation-level Analysis (e.g. ``comparison_matrix``), wired to
every study whose verdict it needs. ``inputs()`` — one ``"node"`` port per
``study_slugs`` entry, wired by the generator to that study's
``StudyStep`` ``result`` store — both orders this step to run AFTER those
studies (the engine's ``determine_steps`` dependency ordering, same
mechanism as ``StudyStep``'s ``prereq_*`` ports) AND delivers each study's
result dict (which carries its ``verdict``) as this step's wired state.

``update()`` assembles ``config_verdicts = {slug: verdict}`` from the wired
study results via ``_extract_study_verdict`` — each ``config_verdicts[slug]``
is the actual verdict dict (``res["analyses"][verdict_analysis]["verdict"]``,
falling back to ``res["verdict"]``, falling back to the raw result), not the
raw ``run_study`` reply. Merges the result into the static ``params``, and
dispatches to the ``run_investigation_analysis`` worker capability (design:
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-investigation-as-composite-design.md,
§Architecture 2-3; refined by
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-store-dataflow-refactor-design.md §2).
Bypasses the parquet-coupled ``run_study_analyses`` path entirely — the
#712 blocker this exists to route around.

NAME: keep this ``InvestigationAnalysisStep``, NOT ``AnalysisStep`` — the
latter collides with ``v2ecoli.workflow.analysis.AnalysisStep`` for the
short link-registry alias in a v2ecoli venv, so ``local:AnalysisStep`` would
silently resolve to the wrong class. The unique name lets the generator use
the plain ``local:InvestigationAnalysisStep`` address safely.

processes.name: JSONEmitter
processes.description: Append simulation state to a persistent JSON file each timestep.

processes.name: ParamVsObservable
processes.description:
Plot reduced observable values across a sweep.

Inputs (declared types):
  sweep_param_values: list[float] — x-axis (one value per run in the sweep)
  reduced_observable: list[float] — y-axis (reduced trajectory per run)

processes.name: PhaseSpace
processes.description:
XY trajectory of two observables.

Inputs (declared types):
  x: list[float]
  y: list[float]

processes.name: RAMEmitter
processes.description:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

processes.name: ResultsStep
processes.description:
The head of the post-sim Step family: reads a finished run's emitted
results location (store path(s), and optionally a sim_data reference)
from config or from a wired-in state input, and writes one
``ResultsHandle`` to the ``results`` store. Every downstream Step —
``AnalysisStep``, ``ReportCardStep``, etc. — reads from that single
handle, so a composite shaped ``[emitter output] -> ResultsStep ->
{AnalysisStep, ReportCardStep, ...}`` gives every post-sim Step the same
view of the run, computed once (``ResultsHandle`` caches its own
``.records()``/``.conn()``, so fan-out doesn't re-read the store).

Config keys (all optional): ``paths`` (list[str]), ``sim_data_ref``
(any), ``simulation_id`` (str). A same-named, non-empty ``state`` input
overrides the matching config key, so a composite can wire an upstream
store (e.g. a run-finished notification carrying the real output path)
instead of hard-coding a path in config.

processes.name: StudyStep
processes.description:
Step base class.

A `Step` is a stateless, non-temporal computational unit within a composite process.
It is triggered when its data dependencies are satisfied, functioning like a reaction
or transformation rule.

Override the `.update()` method to define custom behavior.

Override `.triggers()` to control which input ports trigger the step.
By default all inputs trigger — the step runs whenever any input changes.
To make some inputs "silent" (received but not triggering), return only
the triggering subset from `triggers()`.

Class attributes for memoization:
    ``_cache`` — ``'none'`` (default) or ``'by_hash'``. When
        ``'by_hash'``, ``invoke()`` hashes the Step's config and the
        incoming state, keys a class-level cache by
        ``(schema_version, hash)``, and reuses prior outputs on a
        hit. Requires ``_schema_version``.
    ``_schema_version`` — opaque string identifying the Step's
        output-relevant implementation version. Bumping invalidates
        all prior cache entries under the old version. Required when
        ``_cache == 'by_hash'``.

processes.name: TestReportStep
processes.description:
Evaluate-tail Step: aggregate the run's TestStep verdicts into
report.json and diff against the previous run (diff.json). Emits
``{report, diff, gate}``. ``run_id`` is never generated internally — it
arrives via config/state (workflow-engine ``Date.now()``-free rule).

processes.name: TestStep
processes.description:
A test (formerly "report card") as a visualization-like Step (sibling of
``Analysis`` and ``VisualizationStep``): emits ``view`` (HTML) + ``data``
(verdict map). Unlike ``Analysis`` — which consumes a live DuckDB sim-output
connection — a test's input is a ``StudyContext`` (the study's spec + dir),
so tests grade run-free. Subclasses set ``name`` and implement
``applies(study)`` + ``build(study) -> (verdict_dict, html) | None``. A named
subclass auto-registers in ``TEST_REGISTRY`` and, kind-tagged, in
``POST_SIM_REGISTRY``.

Gating convention: a test's verdict dict is free-form (existing tests are
not required to change), but a test intended to gate a study's Evaluate
stage should shape its verdict as ``{"status": "pass"|"fail"|"warn",
"checks": [...], "summary": <str>}`` so a generic gate can read
``data["status"]`` without knowing the test. ``checks`` is a list of
per-check detail dicts (test-defined shape); ``summary`` is a short
human-readable readout of the verdict.

processes.name: TimeSeriesFromObservables
processes.description:
Multi-observable time series, self-contained.

Config keys (user-set in ``study.yaml.visualizations[].config``):

  - ``observables: list[str]`` (required) — observable names to plot.
    Matched against ``study.yaml.observables[].name`` for units
    + against the ``observables`` map in runs.db ``history.state``
    for data.
  - ``title: str`` (optional) — chart title. Defaults to ``""``.
  - ``sources: list[str]`` (optional) — restrict to runs whose
    ``sim_name`` is in this list. Default: all runs.

Config keys injected by the renderer (private; users don't set
these):

  - ``_runs_db_path: str`` — absolute path to the study's runs.db.
    When absent, the chart renders an empty-data placeholder.
  - ``_study_yaml_path: str`` — absolute path to study.yaml. Used
    to look up per-observable ``units``. When absent, units are
    omitted from axis labels.

Inputs: none (the class plumbs its own data). The renderer's
``build_viz_composite`` skips inputs_map plumbing when a viz class
declares no inputs.

processes.name: TimeSeriesPlot
processes.description:
Plot one or more observables vs time.

Inputs (declared types):
  observable: list[float]   — trajectory values, or list-of-lists for multi-run
  time:       list[float]   — same shape as observable

processes.name: VisualizationStep
processes.description:
A post-sim visualization Step: emits a rendered ``view`` (HTML) + ``data``
(map), like ``Analysis`` but tagged ``kind="visualization"`` so the flush can
route it distinctly. Subclasses set ``name`` and implement
``render(study) -> (html, data) | None``. Inputs default to a StudyContext;
override ``inputs()`` to consume the run extraction instead.

processes.name: edge
processes.description:
Base class for all computational edges in the bigraph schema.

Edges define the interface between simulation processes and the global state,
specifying the structure of input and output ports using bigraph types
(e.g., 'float', 'map[float]', 'list[integer]', etc.).

Upon instantiation, each edge registers its port types with the core.

processes.name: Clock
processes.description:
Emit an integer ``tick`` step counter each update.

(For absolute simulation time, read the engine-maintained ``global_time``
store directly — see the module docstring.)

processes.name: Intervention
processes.description: Apply a specific perturbation to one target store (see module docstring).

processes.name: MathExpressionStep
processes.description:
Evaluate a set of user-configured mathematical expressions as a single Step.

Configuration
-------------
expressions : list[dict]
    List of ``{"out": <str>, "expr": <str>}`` entries. Each ``out`` becomes
    an output port and state field.
params : dict[str, float], optional
    Named constants available to expressions without becoming input ports.
functions : str, optional
    SymPy ``lambdify`` backend module name (default ``"numpy"``).
debug : bool, optional
    If True, prints inferred ports, dependency order, and compilation details.

Notes
-----
Single-pass evaluation in dependency order; not a simultaneous-equation
solver. Cyclic dependencies require a different approach (fixed-point
iteration or root finding).

processes.name: RewriteHandler
processes.description:
Marker base: conformance is checked against the node's wiring, not the
draft's (placeholder) signature.

processes.name: SQLiteEmitter
processes.description:
Append simulation state to a SQLite database each timestep.

One row per step, with the full state tree stored as JSON. The database
file is a single ``.db`` file that can be opened with any SQLite client,
queried with SQL, and kept for long-term storage. Multiple simulations
can share one file — rows are partitioned by ``simulation_id``.

To record the composite config or other metadata alongside the history
rows, call :func:`save_simulation_metadata` after constructing the
Composite — the emitter itself only writes the per-step history rows.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 = every
tick). The ``step`` column still stores the true composite tick number,
so time-series produced from the history reflect the real cadence even
though intermediate ticks were not persisted. Use this when a Composite
fires the emitter very often (small intervals, long runs) and you don't
need every tick in the archive — it's the cheapest way to shrink the
write volume without losing the simulation's time axis.

``batch_size`` buffers up to N recorded rows in memory and flushes them
in a single SQL transaction (default 1 = write each row immediately).
With ``batch_size=100`` the per-row fsync overhead is amortized across
the batch, giving a large speedup on high-frequency runs. Unflushed
rows are guaranteed to be written on ``close()`` and on the next
``query()``; a hard crash before flush loses the buffered rows.
